subject: Re: SIG evidence — CI/CD change-gate clarifications and artifacts
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@sig-audits.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCloud Compliance <compliance@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SIG: evidence request — CI/CD change gates and PR approval trail

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of the SIG questionnaire review for AcmeCloud, they asked for additional artifacts tied to your CI/CD change gate controls: specifically

1) An explanation of how pull request approvals are enforced before merge (roles, required approvers, automation).
2) A short artifact showing the authorization log for PR approvals for a sample release (redact PII).
3) The playbook/runbook that describes emergency change exceptions and rollback steps.

We have an initial assessor call on Friday; can you share the artifacts (or a link) and a one-paragraph summary of the controls by Thursday EOD PST? If any of these are sensitive, indicate redaction and we can handle via secure upload.

Thanks — Oliver
Oliver Grant
Senior Assessor, SIG Audits
oliver.grant@sig-audits.com

--

[Attachment requested: sample auth log (csv); runbook (pdf)]

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@sig-audits.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: evidence request — CI/CD change gates and PR approval trail

Oliver — thanks for the clear ask. We're on it. Quick summary (will expand and attach artifacts):

- PR enforcement: All prod-facing repositories require at least two approvers from different teams (one engineering owner + one security reviewer). Approval rules are enforced by branch protection in GitHub and a required status check from our CI gating pipeline.
- Automation: Merges are blocked until the "ci/change-gate" status check passes; that check validates that unit tests, integration smoke tests, SCA scan, and a signed deployment ticket are present.
- Emergency exceptions: We have a documented emergency flow in the runbook (attached) — post-facto approval required within 24 hours and automatic rollback hooks if verification fails.

I'll attach: a diagram of the CI gating pipeline, the redacted PR approval log CSV (sample), and the runbook PDF. Monica and Karthik will follow up with the exact PR export and any additional audit-profiler logs.

Irene Choi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ci_pipeline_graph.png (png), change-gate-runbook.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: evidence request — PR approval export

Irene / team,

Attached is a redacted export from the approval webhook archive for the release tag v2028.07.01 — contains PR IDs, approver usernames (hashed), timestamps, and approval result. I removed email addresses and any commit diffs.

Notes:
- The approval enforcement is implemented inside our CI gating microservice (auditable): it rejects merges where approver_count < required or where approval_ttl has expired.
- The webhook archive is retained for 365 days; we can provide a signed checksum if the assessor wants tamper-evidence.

Attachment: pr-approval-log.csv

Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@sig-audits.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: AcmeCloud Compliance <compliance@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2028-07-03T13:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: evidence request — follow-ups

Thanks for these — the artifacts look promising. Two quick clarifying questions from the assessor:

1) For the assertion that emergency changes require post-facto approval within 24 hours — can you point to the specific runbook section and show a sample audit entry that demonstrates a post-facto approval being recorded?
2) Does the CI gating check (ci/change-gate) require a signed deployment ticket from a non-committer (i.e., someone other than the PR author)? The assessor wants to confirm separation of duties.

If you can add a single redacted example for each, that would be perfect. We can receive them via the secure drive link.

Oliver

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@sig-audits.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-05T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: evidence request — final clarifications and artifacts uploaded

Oliver — uploaded the requested redacted examples to the secure drive (links below) and included brief notes inline. TL;DR answers: the runbook section 4.2 documents the 24-hour post-facto approval requirement and the workflow; the ci/change-gate requires a deployment-ticket ID that must be signed by an on-call release engineer (non-committer) — the gate rejects a ticket if the signer matches the PR author.

Shared items (secure link, access granted to oliver.grant@sig-audits.com):
- https://secure-upload.redwood.com/sig/ACME/2028-07-change-exceptions.zip
  - contains: emergency_approval_sample.json (redacted audit entry), deployment_ticket_example.pdf (redacted, shows signer role), runbook_excerpt_4_2.pdf

Summary notes included in the upload:
- emergency_approval_sample.json shows the API audit entry with fields: change_id, original_request_ts, emergency_reason, approver_id (hashed), post_facto_approval_ts.
- deployment_ticket_example.pdf shows the ticket metadata and the signer (Release Engineer, sign-in SSO id hashed).

If you need native log formats or signed checksums for the audit archive, say the word and we'll produce them.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Staff Engineer, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments uploaded: emergency_approval_sample.json (txt), deployment_ticket_example.pdf (pdf)
